explanation: I found no Mathlib lemma saying that a self-homeomorphism of a Noetherian space that maps a closed set into itself maps it onto itself. I searched Mathlib/Topology/NoetherianSpace.lean, Homeomorph and Sets/Closeds.lean, and grepped for `image_eq_of_*subset` names and for lemmas combining NoetherianSpace with `≃ₜ`. The closest general tool is `StrictMono.le_apply` in Order/WellFounded.lean: in a `WellFoundedLT` order, a strictly monotone self-map f satisfies x ≤ f x. Mathlib does provide `WellFoundedLT (Closeds X)` for Noetherian spaces. However, it has no map on `Closeds` induced by a homeomorphism (only `IrreducibleCloseds.map`). Using this route would mean building that map on `Closeds X`, proving it is strictly monotone and then turning the result back into the set equation. That takes more than two lines of routine glue, so it does not count as a special case.
